key_facts: Long-term Treasury yields are above 5%; the 10-year traded at 5.19% at the close on Wednesday, up 123 basis points since the end of February. The fiscal 2026 deficit is expected to come in near $2 trillion (CBO estimate: $1.993 trillion), roughly 6.0-6.2% of GDP. Drivers of higher yields cited include the war in Iran (began Feb. 28), rising oil and diesel prices, expectations of possible Fed rate hikes, heavy federal debt issuance, and competition for capital from corporate AI-infrastructure debt. CBO projects the 10-year averaging 4.3% over the next decade versus 5.3% today; rates 0.5 points above CBO's expectations would add $1.9 trillion to 10-year deficits.

Congressional midterms on Nov. 3 are widely expected to produce divided government, with Republicans likely to lose the House and possibly the Senate; the article judges fiscal compromise unlikely in the near term.
